items.prompt: What is the name of the functional group formed when an -OH group is attached to a saturated (sp3) carbon atom?

options.label: Alcohol
Ether
Carboxylic acid
Aldehyde

rubric: An -OH on an sp3 carbon defines an alcohol.
Carboxylic acid is a common confusion because it also contains an OH, but it has a C=O too.

items.prompt: In IUPAC naming, which suffix indicates a carbon-carbon double bond in the parent chain?

options.label: -ol
-ane
-yne
-ene

rubric: -ene marks a C=C double bond.
-yne marks a triple bond and -ane marks only single bonds.

items.prompt: What is the hybridization of each carbon atom in ethene, CH2=CH2?

options.label: sp2
sp
sp3
sp3d

rubric: Each alkene carbon has three sigma bonds and one pi bond, so it is sp2.
sp is for triple bonds and sp3 for four single bonds.

items.prompt: What is the IUPAC name of the unbranched alkane with five carbon atoms?

options.label: Pentane
Propane
Butane
Hexane

rubric: The prefix pent- means five carbons.
Neighbouring names reflect miscounting the prefixes.

items.prompt: Which functional group is represented by the general formula RCHO?

options.label: Ester
Amide
Aldehyde
Ketone

rubric: A carbonyl carbon bonded to H and R is an aldehyde.
A ketone has two carbon groups on the carbonyl carbon.

items.prompt: Which of the following functional groups contain a carbonyl (C=O) group? Select all that apply.

options.label: Amide
Ketone
Alcohol
Ether
Ester

rubric: Ketones, esters and amides all contain C=O.
Ethers and alcohols contain only C-O single bonds.

items.prompt: A student reads the label of a bottle and sees the condensed formula CH3CH2COOH. She wants to name the functional group present at the end of the carbon chain. Which functional group is it?

options.label: Aldehyde, with a C=O at the chain end
Alcohol, with an OH on the end carbon
Ester, with an O-C link at the chain end
Carboxylic acid

rubric: -COOH is the carboxylic acid group.
Ester has an OR group instead of OH; alcohol lacks the C=O.

items.prompt: Why is the shape around the carbon in methane tetrahedral, with bond angles near 109.5 degrees?

options.label: The hydrogen atoms repel each other more strongly than the electron pairs do
Carbon uses one s and one p orbital, which sit at right angles to one another
Carbon has a double bond that forces the hydrogens into a flat arrangement
Four bonding pairs repel each other and spread out as far apart as possible

rubric: Electron-pair repulsion among four sp3 bonds gives a tetrahedron.
Other options confuse hybridization or invent bonding that methane does not have.

items.prompt: Which pair of compounds are constitutional isomers of each other?

options.label: Hexane and methylcyclohexane
Propane and propene
Butane and 2-methylpropane
Ethanol and ethanal

rubric: Both are C4H10 with different connectivity.
The other pairs have different molecular formulas.

items.prompt: Which compound would you predict to be most soluble in water?

options.label: Hexane
Ethanol
Benzene
Pentane

rubric: Ethanol's OH group forms hydrogen bonds with water.
Hydrocarbons are nonpolar and cannot hydrogen bond.

items.prompt: How should 2-propanol, (CH3)2CHOH, be classified?

options.label: Secondary alcohol
Primary alcohol
Tertiary alcohol
Quaternary alcohol

rubric: The carbon bearing OH is bonded to two other carbons, so it is secondary.
Primary would have one carbon attached; tertiary three.

items.prompt: Bromine in CCl4 (red-brown) is added to cyclohexene and the colour disappears quickly. What does this show?

options.label: Br2 added across the C=C double bond
Br2 dissolved in the CCl4 without reacting
Br2 substituted for an H on a ring carbon
Br2 oxidised the ring to an alcohol

rubric: Alkenes undergo addition of Br2, using up the coloured reagent.
Substitution is typical of alkanes and needs light.

items.prompt: Which of the following molecules contain a chiral (stereogenic) carbon? Select all that apply.

options.label: 2-Propanol
2-Chlorobutane
2-Butanol
CHFClBr
Ethanol

rubric: Each correct choice has a carbon bonded to four different groups.
Ethanol and 2-propanol each have a carbon with repeated groups.

items.prompt: In a mechanism drawn in class, a curved arrow starts at a lone pair on a hydroxide ion and points to a carbon atom of an alkyl halide. The instructor asks what this arrow represents. What does it show?

options.label: A bond breaking evenly, with one electron going to each atom
A pair of electrons moving to form a new bond to carbon
A positive charge moving from the carbon toward the oxygen
A single hydrogen atom moving from the oxygen to the carbon

rubric: Curved arrows show movement of electron pairs; this one forms an O-C bond.
Other options confuse arrows with atom movement or radical half-arrows.

items.prompt: What functional group is present in `CH3CH2COCH3`?

options.label: Ketone
Ether
Aldehyde
Ester

rubric: The carbonyl carbon is bonded to two carbons, which makes it a ketone.
Aldehyde is the common mix-up, but an aldehyde carbonyl has at least one H on the carbonyl carbon.

items.prompt: Ethanol (`CH3CH2OH`) boils at 78 °C, but its isomer dimethyl ether (`CH3OCH3`) boils at -24 °C. Which explanation is best?

options.label: Ethanol is partly ionic in the liquid state, so its particles attract each other more strongly than dimethyl ether's do
Ethanol has stronger covalent bonds inside each molecule, and these bonds must break for the liquid to boil
Ethanol has a higher molar mass, so its London forces are far stronger than the forces between dimethyl ether molecules
Ethanol molecules hydrogen-bond to each other, which takes more energy to break than dimethyl ether's weaker forces

rubric: Only ethanol has an O-H group that can donate hydrogen bonds.
The molar mass distractor fails because the two compounds are isomers with the same mass.

items.prompt: Why is a tertiary carbocation more stable than a primary carbocation?

options.label: It has more hydrogens on the charged carbon, so the carbon holds the positive charge more tightly and stays stable
It is less crowded around the charged carbon, so solvent molecules can reach and stabilise the cation more easily
Its alkyl groups withdraw electrons from the carbon, which cancels out the positive charge on that carbon
Its three alkyl groups donate electron density through hyperconjugation and induction, which spreads out the positive charge

rubric: Alkyl groups are electron-donating and stabilise the adjacent positive charge.
Distractors reverse the electronic effect or confuse stability with crowding.

items.prompt: (R)-2-butanol and (S)-2-butanol are best described as which relationship?

options.label: Constitutional isomers
Enantiomers
Diastereomers
Identical compounds

rubric: They are non-superimposable mirror images, so they are enantiomers.
Diastereomers need two or more stereocentres and are not mirror images.

items.prompt: A chiral secondary alkyl bromide reacts with a good nucleophile in a single concerted SN2 step. What happens at the stereocentre?

options.label: It becomes planar and stays planar
Its configuration is retained
Its configuration is inverted
It gives a 50:50 racemic mixture

rubric: Backside attack in SN2 inverts the configuration.
Racemisation and retention are features of SN1 or other mechanisms, not concerted SN2.

items.prompt: Which of these molecules are chiral? Select all that apply.

options.label: 3-bromopentane
2-bromobutane
2-propanol
1-bromobutane
`CHBrClF`

rubric: Each correct choice has a carbon with four different groups.
3-Bromopentane, 2-propanol and 1-bromobutane have no carbon bearing four different groups.

items.prompt: A student adds HBr to propene and finds that the main product is 2-bromopropane, not 1-bromopropane. Her instructor asks her to explain this result using the mechanism.

options.label: The two products form at equal rates, but 1-bromopropane evaporates because it is more volatile during the work-up
Bromine is more electronegative than hydrogen, so it always bonds to the carbon with fewer hydrogens in any addition
Protonation of the alkene gives a secondary carbocation, which is more stable than the primary one, so Br- attacks C2
Protonation gives a primary carbocation first, which then rearranges by a methyl shift so Br- can attack C2

rubric: Markovnikov selectivity follows from the more stable carbocation intermediate.
Distractors invent a rule, a wrong rearrangement, or a work-up artefact.

items.prompt: What is the IUPAC name of `CH3CH(CH3)CH2CH2OH`?

options.label: 2-methylbutan-1-ol
3-methylbutan-1-ol
2-methylbutan-4-ol
3-methylbutan-2-ol

rubric: Number the chain from the end nearest the OH, which places OH at C1 and the methyl at C3.
Other options number from the wrong end or misplace a group.

items.prompt: 2-Butanol is treated with an oxidising agent such as `Na2Cr2O7, H2SO4`. What is the main organic product?

options.label: Butanal
2-Butene
Butanoic acid
Butanone

rubric: A secondary alcohol is oxidised to a ketone and cannot be oxidised further.
Butanal and butanoic acid would come from a primary alcohol.

items.prompt: 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane is heated with KOH in ethanol and undergoes E2 elimination. What is the major alkene product?

options.label: 2-Methylbut-2-ene
2-Methylbutan-2-ol
2-Methylbut-1-ene
3-Methylbut-1-ene

rubric: Zaitsev's rule favours the more substituted alkene.
2-Methylbut-1-ene is the less substituted Hofmann-type product, and the alcohol is a substitution product.

items.prompt: Cyclohexanone is treated with `NaBH4` in methanol, then a mild aqueous work-up. What is the product?

options.label: Hexanoic acid
Cyclohexene
Cyclohexanol
Cyclohexane

rubric: NaBH4 reduces a ketone to a secondary alcohol.
Cyclohexane would need complete deoxygenation, and the acid would need oxidation and ring opening.

items.prompt: Which reagent sequence converts 1-butene into 1-butanol (anti-Markovnikov hydration)?

options.label: 1. `Hg(OAc)2, H2O`; 2. `NaBH4`
1. `BH3·THF`; 2. `H2O2, NaOH`
1. `HBr`; 2. `NaOH`
`H2O, H2SO4`

rubric: Hydroboration-oxidation puts OH on the less substituted carbon.
Acid hydration and oxymercuration give 2-butanol, and HBr followed by NaOH also gives the 2-substituted product.

items.prompt: Each alkyl bromide is treated with `NaCN` in DMSO. Which ones will undergo SN2 substitution readily? Select all that apply.

options.label: 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane
Bromomethane
1-Bromopropane
1-Bromo-2,2-dimethylpropane

rubric: SN2 works readily at unhindered methyl and primary carbons.
The tertiary bromide and the highly hindered neopentyl bromide are too crowded for backside attack.

items.prompt: In the lab, a student bubbles 1-butene through a solution of `Br2` in `CH2Cl2` at room temperature. The red-brown colour of bromine fades quickly. The student has to identify the main organic product.

options.label: 1,2-Dibromobutane
1,1-Dibromobutane
2,2-Dibromobutane
2-Bromobutane

rubric: Br2 adds across the double bond through a bromonium ion, giving a vicinal dibromide.
Geminal dibromides and the monobromide do not form in this addition.

items.prompt: Which major product forms when 2-methylbut-2-ene reacts with HBr (no peroxides)?

options.label: 1-bromo-2-methylbutane
2-bromo-3-methylbutane
1-bromo-3-methylbutane
2-bromo-2-methylbutane

rubric: Markovnikov addition places Br on the more substituted carbon via the tertiary carbocation.
Other options reflect anti-Markovnikov placement or a misnumbered secondary product.

items.prompt: Which reagent sequence converts 1-butene into butan-1-ol?

options.label: HBr, then NaOH(aq) in water with heat
1) Hg(OAc)2, H2O; 2) NaBH4
1) BH3·THF; 2) H2O2, NaOH
H2O, H2SO4 (acid-catalysed hydration)

rubric: Hydroboration-oxidation gives anti-Markovnikov alcohol, the primary alcohol.
Acid hydration and oxymercuration give Markovnikov butan-2-ol.

items.prompt: What is the major product of (CH3)3C-Br with sodium ethoxide in ethanol at 55 °C?

options.label: 1-bromo-2-methylpropane
2-methylpropan-2-ol
2-methylpropene
tert-butyl ethyl ether

rubric: A tertiary halide with a strong base undergoes E2 elimination to the alkene.
Ether is the SN2/SN1 product, which is disfavoured here by sterics and base strength.

items.prompt: What is the product of treating propan-2-ol with PCC in dichloromethane?

options.label: Propanoic acid
Propanone
Propene
Propanal

rubric: PCC oxidises a secondary alcohol to a ketone.
Propanal and propanoic acid would need a primary alcohol; propene would need dehydration.

items.prompt: Which reagent combination converts bromoethane into propanenitrile, extending the carbon chain by one?

options.label: NaBr in acetone
NaOH in water
CH3ONa in methanol
NaCN in DMSO

rubric: Cyanide is a carbon nucleophile that displaces bromide by SN2.
Other reagents give alcohol, no change, or methyl ethyl ether.

items.prompt: Which reagents convert benzene directly into a substituted benzene through electrophilic aromatic substitution? Select all that apply.

options.label: HNO3 with H2SO4 giving nitrobenzene
H2 with Pd/C giving cyclohexane
Br2 with FeBr3 giving bromobenzene
NaOH with CH3Cl giving toluene by nucleophilic attack on the ring

items.prompt: A student adds CH3MgBr in dry ether to propanone, then performs a mild aqueous acid workup. Which product does she obtain?

options.label: A secondary alcohol, propan-2-ol, from hydride delivery to the carbonyl
A tertiary alcohol with four carbons, (CH3)3COH, after methyl addition
A ketone, butan-2-one, from methyl substitution at the carbonyl carbon
A secondary alcohol, butan-2-ol, from methyl addition then loss of water

items.prompt: An SN2 reaction of 2-bromobutane with NaCN in DMSO gives optically active (R)-nitrile from (S)-bromide. Racemic product forms in ethanol/water instead. What best explains the change?

options.label: DMSO stabilises the leaving group through hydrogen bonding, so substitution proceeds with retention of configuration
Ethanol solvates the nucleophile on one face only, so cyanide can attack from the front side as well as the back
Protic solvent favours a carbocation (SN1) pathway, which loses stereochemical information
Protic solvent strengthens the cyanide nucleophile by hydrogen bonding, so backside attack is faster and less selective

rubric: Polar protic solvents stabilise ionic intermediates and favour SN1, giving racemisation.
Protic solvents actually solvate and weaken anionic nucleophiles.

items.prompt: Treating 3-methylbutan-2-ol with concentrated H2SO4 and heat gives mainly 2-methylbut-2-ene, not 3-methylbut-1-ene. Which step explains this?

options.label: The alcohol is oxidised to a ketone first, and the ketone then loses water
Water adds back to the protonated alcohol to form a stable ether that then eliminates
A 1,2-hydride shift gives a tertiary carbocation before a proton is lost
Direct E2 by bisulfate removes the least hindered hydrogen at C1 in one concerted step

rubric: Secondary carbocation rearranges by hydride shift to tertiary, then Zaitsev elimination.
E2 and oxidation do not apply under these E1 acidic conditions.

items.prompt: Nitration of toluene gives mostly ortho and para products, while nitration of nitrobenzene gives mostly meta. What explains the difference?

options.label: Methyl withdraws inductively, so it directs the nitronium ion to the ring positions with the most electron density
Methyl is bulky and blocks the meta position, while the smaller nitro group leaves the ortho and para sites hindered
Nitro donates electrons by resonance to the meta position, making that carbon the most nucleophilic site
Methyl stabilises the arenium ion from ortho/para attack, while nitro destabilises it

rubric: Donors stabilise positive charge adjacent to the substituent in ortho/para intermediates; withdrawers destabilise it, leaving meta least bad.
Sterics are not the cause, and nitro is a withdrawing group.

items.prompt: A chemist tries to make a tertiary alcohol with a Grignard reagent in ether, but the starting ketone also has a free -OH group and the yield is almost zero. What is the most likely cause?

options.label: The ketone carbonyl is too hindered for any nucleophile to attack
Ether solvent slowly oxidises the Grignard reagent before it adds
The alcohol reacts with the ketone to form a stable hemiacetal
Acidic O-H protonates the Grignard reagent, destroying it

rubric: Grignards are strong bases and are quenched by O-H protons, so the group needs protection.
Other options invent processes not typical for this system.

items.prompt: Two bottles contain either pentan-2-one or pentanal. IR shows C=O near 1715 cm^-1, and Tollens' reagent gives no silver mirror. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.label: It is pentanal, because aldehydes resist oxidation by mild oxidants
It is pentan-2-one, because ketones resist mild oxidation
It is pentan-2-one, because the C=O stretch is absent in ketones at that position
It is pentanal, because the C=O frequency is too low for a ketone

rubric: Tollens' oxidises aldehydes only; a negative test indicates a ketone.
Aldehydes oxidise readily, and ketones do show strong C=O bands.

items.prompt: A student's SN2 reaction of 1-bromobutane with sodium azide in acetone is far slower than expected. Which observations would identify a likely cause? Select all that apply.

options.label: The azide salt was poorly soluble and mostly undissolved
The substrate was actually 2-bromo-2-methylpropane
The solvent was found to contain substantial water
The reaction was run at a slightly warmer temperature

rubric: Water solvates the nucleophile, low solubility lowers concentration, and a tertiary halide resists SN2.
Warmer temperature would speed the reaction, not slow it.

items.prompt: A chemist brominates ethylbenzene with Br2 and FeBr3 and obtains ortho and para bromoethylbenzene. Later she uses Br2 with light and obtains (1-bromoethyl)benzene instead. Why does the bromine end up in different places?

options.label: Light makes the ring more nucleophilic, so Br2 adds to the ring faster than to the side chain
FeBr3 generates bromine radicals that abstract the benzylic hydrogen, while light polarises Br2 to attack the ring
FeBr3 makes an electrophile for ring substitution; light makes Br radicals that abstract the weak benzylic H
Under light the ethyl group switches from electron-donating to withdrawing, so ring attack stops and the side chain reacts

rubric: Lewis acid gives electrophilic aromatic substitution; light gives radical benzylic bromination at the weakest C-H.
Other options swap the roles of the conditions.

items.prompt: Neopentyl bromide, (CH3)3CCH2Br, is nearly inert to NaOEt in ethanol at 25 C (SN2 conditions) and to simple ethanol solvolysis (SN1 conditions). Which analysis explains both failures?

options.label: SN2 is slowed by electron donation from the three methyl groups to the reacting carbon, and SN1 fails because ethanol cannot solvate ions
SN2 needs a tertiary carbon to stabilise its transition state, and SN1 fails because three methyl groups raise the carbocation energy
SN2 is blocked because primary halides cannot be attacked from behind, and SN1 fails because bromide is a very poor leaving group
SN2 is blocked because the adjacent quaternary carbon shields the backside, and SN1 would require an unstable primary carbocation

rubric: Branching at the beta carbon blocks the SN2 trajectory, and ionisation would give a primary cation, so both pathways are slow.
Distractors misstate primary-halide reactivity or leaving-group ability, or confuse alpha and beta branching.

items.prompt: In the locked chair of 4-tert-butylcyclohexyl bromide, the cis isomer undergoes E2 with KOtBu much faster than the trans isomer. Which analysis explains this?

options.label: In the cis isomer the tert-butyl group is axial, which stabilises the developing carbocation and lowers the barrier for loss of Br
In the cis isomer Br sits equatorial and is less hindered, so it leaves more readily under the strongly basic conditions
In the trans isomer Br is axial and suffers 1,3-diaxial strain, which should make it the faster eliminator rather than the cis
In the cis isomer the equatorial tert-butyl forces Br axial, so axial H atoms on adjacent carbons are anti-periplanar to C-Br

rubric: E2 needs an anti-periplanar H and leaving group, which in a chair means both axial; cis places Br axial when tBu is equatorial.
Distractors invoke ground-state strain or carbocations, ignoring the stereoelectronic requirement.

items.prompt: 1-Methylcyclohexene is treated with BH3 in THF, then H2O2/NaOH. The main product is trans-2-methylcyclohexanol, not 1-methylcyclohexanol. Which mechanistic feature accounts for both the regiochemistry and the stereochemistry?

options.label: A radical chain places boron on the more substituted carbon, and the less hindered face is then attacked by hydroxide
Concerted syn addition of B-H places boron on the less hindered carbon, and oxidation replaces B with OH with retention
A tertiary carbocation forms first, water attacks it from the less hindered face, and the OH ends up trans to methyl
A cyclic bromonium-like boron intermediate forces anti addition of H and B, so the OH is trans to the added hydrogen

rubric: Concerted syn addition puts H on C1 and B on C2 on the same face, so after retentive oxidation OH is trans to methyl.
Distractors import carbocation, bridged-ion or radical mechanisms from other alkene additions.

items.prompt: A compound C5H10O shows a strong IR band at 1715 cm^-1 and no band near 2720 cm^-1. Its 1H NMR shows only a triplet (6H, delta 1.05) and a quartet (4H, delta 2.45). Which structure fits?

options.label: 3-Methylbutan-2-one
Pentan-2-one
Pentan-3-one
Pentanal

rubric: Two equivalent ethyl groups flanking a ketone C=O give only one triplet and one quartet.
Pentan-2-one and 3-methylbutan-2-one would show a methyl singlet; pentanal would show an aldehyde C-H.

items.prompt: p-Nitrophenol (pKa about 7.2) is noticeably more acidic than m-nitrophenol (pKa about 8.4), although nitro is electron-withdrawing at both positions. Which analysis best accounts for the difference?

options.label: The nitro group at meta is closer to the oxygen, so it donates electron density by resonance and destabilises the phenoxide
In the para phenoxide the negative charge delocalises onto the nitro oxygens, while no such resonance form exists for meta
The inductive effect is stronger at the para position because it acts through the ring pi system over a longer distance
The para nitro group hydrogen-bonds intramolecularly to the OH proton, which stabilises the anion after deprotonation

rubric: Only para (and ortho) nitro can accept charge by resonance from the phenoxide oxygen; meta gets only the inductive effect.
Distractors misassign resonance donation, intramolecular H-bonding (an ortho effect) or inductive distance dependence.

items.prompt: A chemist studies solvolysis of a secondary alkyl bromide in aqueous ethanol and wants evidence that the mechanism is SN1 rather than SN2. Which observations point to SN1? Select all that apply.

options.label: A single product forms with complete inversion of configuration at the stereocentre
The rate increases when the solvent is changed from aqueous ethanol to pure acetone
A product with a rearranged carbon skeleton is isolated alongside the expected substitution product
The rate does not change when the concentration of the added nucleophile is doubled

rubric: Zero order in nucleophile and rearrangement both indicate a carbocation intermediate.
Moving to acetone disfavours ionisation, and clean inversion is the SN2 signature.

items.prompt: A student adds magnesium turnings to 3-bromopropan-1-ol in rigorously dry diethyl ether. After the metal is consumed, she bubbles in CO2 and acidifies, hoping for 4-hydroxybutanoic acid. She isolates mainly propan-1-ol. What best explains this outcome?

options.label: The O-H group protonates the Grignard reagent as soon as it forms, so the carbanion is quenched before CO2 is added
The magnesium oxide coating prevents insertion into C-Br bonds, so the starting material is simply recovered as the alcohol
CO2 is too weakly electrophilic to react with any Grignard reagent, so only the protonated alkane-type product forms
The alkyl bromide undergoes Wurtz-type coupling on the metal surface, which converts the chain into hexane-1,6-diol

rubric: An alcohol O-H is far more acidic than the conjugate acid of a carbanion, so the Grignard is destroyed by proton transfer.
Distractors blame CO2 reactivity, coupling or the metal surface rather than the incompatible functional group.

items.prompt: 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane must be converted mainly to the less substituted alkene, 2-methylbut-1-ene. Criteria: E2 conditions, maximum Hofmann selectivity, minimal substitution. Which conditions are best?

options.label: Water at 80 C, since a neutral solvent avoids the stronger-base competition
NaOEt in ethanol at 55 C, since a small base removes the most accessible proton
KOtBu in tert-butanol, since a bulky base removes the less hindered proton
NaCN in DMSO at 25 C, since a strong nucleophile promotes clean elimination

rubric: A bulky base favours the sterically accessible methyl hydrogen, giving the Hofmann product, and cannot easily substitute at a tertiary carbon.
NaOEt gives the Zaitsev alkene, water gives SN1/E1 mixtures, and cyanide is a nucleophile, not a selective base.

items.prompt: Criteria: convert 1-bromobutane into butan-1-amine (same carbon count) with minimal over-alkylation to secondary and tertiary amines, using reliable, well-precedented steps. Which route is best?

options.label: Treat with NaCN, then reduce with LiAlH4, since nitrile reduction gives a primary amine selectively and avoids any alkylation of the product
Treat with one equivalent of NH3 in ethanol, since limiting the nucleophile prevents further alkylation of the product amine
Treat with NaNH2 in liquid ammonia, since the amide anion is a stronger nucleophile than ammonia and reacts faster than the product
Treat with potassium phthalimide, then hydrazine, since the imide N can be alkylated only once

rubric: Gabriel synthesis alkylates a nitrogen that cannot be alkylated twice, then releases the primary amine without chain change.
Direct ammonia alkylation over-alkylates, the nitrile route adds a carbon, and NaNH2 mainly causes elimination.

items.prompt: A keto-ester must have only the ester reduced to a primary alcohol, leaving the ketone as it is. Criteria: high selectivity, reagents available in any lab, acceptable step count. Which plan is best?

options.label: Use H2 over Pd/C, since catalytic hydrogenation reduces esters more readily than ketones
Use one equivalent of LiAlH4 at -78 C, since low temperature makes ester reduction faster than ketone reduction
Protect the ketone as a cyclic acetal, reduce with LiAlH4, then remove the acetal with aqueous acid
Use NaBH4 in methanol, since it is the mildest hydride and leaves carbonyl groups untouched

rubric: Ketones are more reactive than esters toward hydrides, so the ketone must be masked with an acetal, which is stable to LiAlH4.
NaBH4 reduces the ketone and not the ester, and the other two options reverse the true reactivity order.

items.prompt: A student plans to make propylbenzene by treating benzene with 1-chloropropane and AlCl3. Criteria: the product must be the straight-chain isomer in good yield and be free of polyalkylation. Which critique and alternative are best?

options.label: The plan gives rearranged product, so use a larger excess of 1-chloropropane to push the reaction to the straight-chain isomer
The plan is sound, since a primary chloride gives a primary cation that attacks benzene without further change
The plan fails because AlCl3 deactivates benzene, so use FeBr3 instead to promote alkylation with the same chloride
The plan gives rearranged isopropylbenzene and polyalkylation; instead acylate with propanoyl chloride/AlCl3 and reduce the ketone

rubric: Alkylation suffers hydride-shift rearrangement and the product is more reactive than benzene; acylation avoids both, and Clemmensen or Wolff-Kishner then gives propylbenzene.
Other options misjudge carbocation behaviour or the role of the catalyst.

items.prompt: 2,2-Dimethyloxirane must be converted to 1-methoxy-2-methylpropan-2-ol (methoxide attacking the CH2 carbon). Criteria: high regioselectivity for the less hindered carbon, no acid-sensitive side products. Which conditions are best?

options.label: BF3 in methanol, since the Lewis acid directs methanol to the less hindered carbon
Neat methanol at 25 C, since the neutral nucleophile attacks the less hindered carbon selectively
NaOMe in methanol, since the strong nucleophile opens the ring by SN2 at the CH2 carbon
Catalytic H2SO4 in methanol, since protonation makes the more substituted carbon the site of attack

rubric: Under basic conditions, ring opening is SN2-like at the less substituted carbon, giving the target.
Acidic conditions shift attack to the tertiary carbon, and neutral methanol is too weak to open the epoxide at 25 C.

items.prompt: A molecule contains a ketone and an isolated C=C double bond. Criteria: convert the ketone to a secondary alcohol, keep the C=C intact, use one step. Which reagents meet all criteria? Select all that apply.

options.label: H2 with Pd/C in ethanol
LiAlH4 in ether, then aqueous workup
Zn(Hg), HCl (Clemmensen conditions)
NaBH4 in methanol

rubric: Both hydrides reduce ketones to alcohols and do not reduce isolated alkenes.
Pd/C hydrogenates the alkene, and Clemmensen gives a CH2 group rather than an alcohol.

items.prompt: A process chemist must make tert-butyl methyl ether by a Williamson synthesis. Two routes are proposed. Criteria: maximise ether yield, minimise alkene by-product, use ordinary reagents. Which route should she choose?

options.label: Sodium tert-butoxide with tert-butyl chloride, since matching the alkyl groups avoids any mixed-ether by-product problem
Sodium hydroxide with methanol and tert-butanol, since the hydroxide deprotonates both alcohols to make the ether directly
Sodium tert-butoxide with iodomethane, since SN2 at a methyl carbon is unhindered and cannot compete with elimination
Sodium methoxide with tert-butyl chloride, since the tertiary halide ionises readily and methoxide traps it

rubric: A methyl halide undergoes SN2 with a bulky alkoxide without any beta hydrogens to eliminate, so the ether forms cleanly.
Methoxide with a tertiary halide mainly gives E2 isobutene, and the other options do not form the unsymmetrical ether selectively.

items.prompt: You need the substitution product from 2-bromobutane and azide, with minimal elimination and clean inversion of configuration. Judged against these criteria, which conditions are best?

options.label: NaN3 in methanol at reflux, since a protic solvent stabilises the leaving group and speeds backside attack
KOtBu in tBuOH at 25 °C, since a bulky strong base promotes backside attack at the secondary carbon
NaN3 in DMF at 25 °C, since azide is a good, weakly basic nucleophile and DMF leaves it unsolvated
NaN3 in water with AgNO3, since silver assists ionisation and ensures a clean inversion pathway

rubric: Azide is a strong nucleophile but weak base, and a polar aprotic solvent favours a clean SN2 pathway at a secondary centre.
Silver and protic solvents push the reaction toward SN1 and loss of stereochemical control, and bulky bases favour E2.

items.prompt: HBr adds to 1,3-butadiene to give mainly 3-bromobut-1-ene at −80 °C but mainly 1-bromobut-2-ene after the mixture is warmed to 40 °C. Which evaluation of this observation is best supported?

options.label: At −80 °C the faster-forming 1,2-adduct is trapped, while at 40 °C ionisation is reversible so the more stable internal alkene accumulates
The 1,4-adduct always forms through the lower-energy transition state at every temperature, and heating only raises its rate relative to the 1,2-adduct, so it overtakes the 1,2-adduct
Heating converts the 1,4-adduct into the 1,2-adduct because the terminal alkene is the more stable product at equilibrium, so the 1,2-adduct dominates when warmed
At −80 °C the allylic cation is attacked at the carbon bearing less charge, whereas at 40 °C the charge distribution reverses to favour attack at C4 instead

rubric: This is kinetic versus thermodynamic control: the 1,2-adduct forms faster, and the disubstituted 1,4-alkene wins once equilibration is possible.
Distractors reverse the stability order or claim that the transition-state preference changes with temperature.

items.prompt: A keto ester must have its ester reduced to a primary alcohol while its ketone survives unchanged. Judged against this chemoselectivity goal, which plan is best?

options.label: Protect the ketone as a cyclic ketal, reduce with NaBH4, then deprotect, since ketals are inert to hydride reagents
Protect the ketone as a cyclic ketal, reduce with LiAlH4, then deprotect with aqueous acid, since ketals resist hydride attack
Treat directly with NaBH4 in methanol, since the milder hydride reduces esters faster than ketones
Treat directly with LiAlH4 at −78 °C, since the low temperature makes the ester more electrophilic than the ketone

rubric: Ketals are stable to LiAlH4, which is strong enough to reduce the ester; aqueous acid then restores the ketone.
NaBH4 does not reduce simple esters, and ketones are intrinsically more reactive than esters toward hydride, so direct reduction fails.

items.prompt: 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane should give mainly the less substituted alkene, 2-methylbut-1-ene, by E2. Judged against that criterion, which base and solvent are best?

options.label: NaOEt in ethanol, since a small base removes the most substituted hydrogen and gives the more stable alkene
KOtBu in tBuOH, since the bulky base removes the more accessible methyl hydrogen faster
NaOH in aqueous acetone, since hydroxide is small and favours the less hindered hydrogen
Water with gentle heating, since a weak base selects the least substituted alkene through E1

rubric: A hindered base favours Hofmann-type elimination by abstracting the sterically accessible hydrogen.
Small bases and E1 conditions follow Zaitsev selectivity and give the more substituted alkene.

items.prompt: An allylic alcohol must be converted in one step into an enantioenriched epoxy alcohol, with the face of attack set by the choice of reagent rather than by the substrate. Which method best meets this criterion?

options.label: Br2 in water, then NaOH, since anti addition and ring closure fix the absolute configuration
OsO4 with NMO, since syn dihydroxylation of the alkene gives one enantiomer of the epoxide
mCPBA in CH2Cl2, since the peracid approaches the less hindered face and always delivers a single enantiomer
Ti(OiPr)4, tBuOOH and chiral diethyl tartrate, since the chiral titanium complex directs oxygen to one face

rubric: Sharpless epoxidation uses a chiral tartrate-titanium catalyst to control which face is epoxidised, independent of the substrate.
Achiral reagents give racemic product from an achiral substrate, and OsO4 gives diols rather than epoxides.

items.prompt: 2-Methylcyclohexanone is treated with a slight excess of LDA in THF at −78 °C and then trapped with TMSCl, giving mainly the less substituted silyl enol ether. Which statements correctly explain this selectivity? Select all that apply.

options.label: Using a slight excess of ketone over base would reinforce selectivity by allowing proton exchange between enolates.
Deprotonation is effectively irreversible at low temperature, so the ratio reflects relative rates rather than enolate stability.
Complete conversion with slight excess base prevents proton transfer from unreacted ketone that would equilibrate the enolates.
The bulky base removes the more accessible CH2 hydrogen faster than the hindered methine hydrogen.
The less substituted enolate is the more stable alkene, so equilibration drives the outcome.

rubric: Kinetic enolate formation depends on a hindered strong base, low temperature and irreversible deprotonation, with no leftover ketone to equilibrate.
Distractors invoke thermodynamic control or ketone excess, both of which erode kinetic selectivity.

items.prompt: A chemist treats enantiopure (R)-2-bromooctane with NaN3 in 80:20 ethanol/water at 80 °C. The 2-azidooctane obtained is only 35% ee, mostly inverted. The goal is maximum enantiopurity. Which change is best?

options.label: Raise the temperature to 120 °C so the faster bimolecular pathway outcompetes ionisation of the bromide
Switch to DMF at 25 °C with excess azide, keeping the reaction bimolecular
Add AgBF4 to speed up bromide loss and push the mixture toward a pure inversion pathway
Increase the water content to stabilise the transition state and so improve inversion at carbon

rubric: Partial racemisation signals competing SN1 or ion-pair chemistry; polar aprotic solvent, lower temperature and high nucleophile concentration favour pure SN2 inversion.
Heat, silver salts and more water all promote ionisation and further erode stereochemical purity.

items.prompt: Starting only from acetylene and bromoethane as carbon sources, which sequence best prepares (Z)-hex-3-ene?

options.label: NaNH2 then EtBr, repeated once, then H2 over Pd/C
NaNH2 then EtBr, repeated once, then H2 over Lindlar catalyst
NaNH2 then EtBr, repeated once, then Na in liquid NH3
NaOH then EtBr, repeated once, then H2 over Lindlar catalyst

rubric: Double alkylation of the acetylide builds hex-3-yne, and Lindlar hydrogenation delivers syn addition to the cis alkene.
Pd/C over-reduces to the alkane, Na/NH3 gives the E alkene, and NaOH is too weak to deprotonate a terminal alkyne.

items.prompt: Which reagent sequence converts 1-methylcyclohexene into racemic trans-2-methylcyclohexanol?

options.label: OsO4 with NMO, then NaHSO3
Hg(OAc)2 in water, then NaBH4
BH3·THF, then H2O2 with NaOH
Dilute H2SO4 in water

rubric: Hydroboration-oxidation adds H and OH syn with the OH at the less substituted carbon, giving the trans relationship between methyl and OH.
Oxymercuration and acid hydration give the tertiary alcohol, and OsO4 gives a diol.

items.prompt: 3-Phenylpentan-3-ol must be made in one pot from one carbonyl compound and one Grignard reagent, with no ketone left over. Which pair meets this?

options.label: Ethyl benzoate with at least 2 equivalents of EtMgBr, then aqueous acid
Ethyl propanoate with at least 2 equivalents of PhMgBr, then aqueous acid
Benzaldehyde with 2 equivalents of EtMgBr, then aqueous acid
Ethyl benzoate with exactly 1 equivalent of EtMgBr at −78 °C, then aqueous acid

rubric: An ester adds two identical groups from the Grignard reagent, giving Ph-C(OH)(Et)2 after workup.
The propanoate route would give a diphenyl carbinol, one equivalent stops at a ketone mixture, and an aldehyde gives a secondary alcohol.

items.prompt: A chemist wants mainly the 'para' regioisomer, 4-methylcyclohex-3-ene-1-carbaldehyde, from a thermal Diels-Alder reaction. Which diene and dienophile best fit by frontier orbital control?

options.label: Butadiene with crotonaldehyde, since the β-methyl dienophile directs a 'para' product
trans-Piperylene with acrolein, since the 1-substituted diene places the methyl 'para' to the aldehyde
2,3-Dimethylbutadiene with acrolein, since two methyl groups sharpen the para selectivity
Isoprene with acrolein, since the 2-substituted diene's largest HOMO coefficient at C1 matches the β-carbon

rubric: 2-Substituted dienes with electron-withdrawing dienophiles give the 'para' product, so isoprene plus acrolein fits.
1-Substituted dienes give the 'ortho' product, and the other pairs cannot produce this substitution pattern.

items.prompt: Which sequence best converts benzene into 1-bromo-3-propylbenzene?

options.label: 1-Chloropropane/AlCl3; then Br2/FeBr3
Propanoyl chloride/AlCl3; then Br2/FeBr3; then Zn(Hg)/HCl
Br2/FeBr3; then propanoyl chloride/AlCl3; then Zn(Hg)/HCl
Propanoyl chloride/AlCl3; then Zn(Hg)/HCl; then Br2/FeBr3

rubric: The acyl group is meta-directing, so brominate before reducing the ketone to the propyl group.
Direct alkylation rearranges and directs ortho/para, and the other orders place bromine para or ortho to propyl.

items.prompt: A proposed route to 4-acetylbenzoic acid treats 4-bromoacetophenone with Mg in dry ether, bubbles in CO2, then quenches. The plan is flawed. Which changes would make it work? Select all that apply.

options.label: Replace Mg with lithium metal, since the aryllithium would not attack the ketone.
Protect the ketone as a cyclic ketal before forming the Grignard reagent.
Finish with an aqueous acid workup, which protonates the carboxylate and removes the ketal.
Run the Grignard formation in aqueous THF so CO2 is trapped as carbonic acid.
Add 2 equivalents of Mg so the excess metal protects the ketone in situ.

rubric: A Grignard reagent would attack the ketone, so it must be masked as a ketal, and acid workup both protonates the carboxylate and removes the ketal.
Organolithiums are even more reactive toward ketones, excess Mg does not protect anything, and water destroys Grignard reagents.

items.prompt: A chemist must convert (R)-2-octanol into (R)-2-azidooctane, which requires net retention of configuration, and wants to avoid any SN1 chemistry. Which plan satisfies this?

options.label: Treat with PPh3, DEAD and HN3 under Mitsunobu conditions, giving retention through a phosphonium intermediate
Heat with NaN3 in aqueous H2SO4, giving retention via a planar cation attacked from the original face
Make the tosylate, displace with NaI in acetone, then displace the iodide with NaN3 in DMF, giving two inversions
Make the tosylate, then displace directly with NaN3 in DMF, giving retention through a tight ion pair

rubric: Two sequential SN2 inversions give net retention without carbocation involvement.
A single SN2 step or a Mitsunobu reaction gives inversion, and SN1 conditions would give racemisation.
